work.title: The Second Part of King Henry the Fourth
work.author: William Shakespeare

scene.label: Act 4, Scene 2
scene.title: SCENE II. Another part of the forest.

content.text: Enter, from one side, Mowbray, attended; afterwards, the Archbishop, Hastings, and others; from the other side, Prince John of Lancaster, and Westmoreland; Officers, and others with them.

lines.text: You are well encounter'd here, my cousin Mowbray.
lines.plainText: You are well encounter'd here my cousin Mowbray

lines.text: Good day to you, gentle Lord Archbishop;
lines.plainText: Good day to you gentle Lord Archbishop

lines.text: And so to you, Lord Hastings, and to all.
lines.plainText: And so to you Lord Hastings and to all

lines.text: My Lord of York, it better show'd with you
lines.plainText: My Lord of York it better show'd with you

lines.text: When that your flock, assembled by the bell,
lines.plainText: When that your flock assembled by the bell

lines.text: Encircled you to hear with reverence
lines.plainText: Encircled you to hear with reverence

lines.text: Your exposition on the holy text
lines.plainText: Your exposition on the holy text

lines.text: Than now to see you here an iron man,
lines.plainText: Than now to see you here an iron man

lines.text: Cheering a rout of rebels with your drum,
lines.plainText: Cheering a rout of rebels with your drum

lines.text: Turning the word to sword, and life to death.
lines.plainText: Turning the word to sword and life to death

lines.text: That man that sits within a monarch's heart,
lines.plainText: That man that sits within a monarch's heart

lines.text: And ripens in the sunshine of his favour,
lines.plainText: And ripens in the sunshine of his favour

lines.text: Would he abuse the countenance of the king,
lines.plainText: Would he abuse the countenance of the king

lines.text: Alack, what mischiefs might he set abroach
lines.plainText: Alack what mischiefs might he set abroach

lines.text: In shadow of such greatness! With you, Lord Bishop,
lines.plainText: In shadow of such greatness With you Lord Bishop

lines.text: It is even so. Who hath not heard it spoken
lines.plainText: It is even so Who hath not heard it spoken

lines.text: How deep you were within the books of God,
lines.plainText: How deep you were within the books of God

lines.text: To us the speaker in his parliament,
lines.plainText: To us the speaker in his parliament

lines.text: To us th' imagined voice of God himself,
lines.plainText: To us th' imagined voice of God himself

lines.text: The very opener and intelligencer
lines.plainText: The very opener and intelligencer

lines.text: Between the grace, the sanctities of heaven,
lines.plainText: Between the grace the sanctities of heaven

lines.text: And our dull workings? O, who shall believe
lines.plainText: And our dull workings O who shall believe

lines.text: But you misuse the reverence of your place,
lines.plainText: But you misuse the reverence of your place

lines.text: Employ the countenance and grace of heaven
lines.plainText: Employ the countenance and grace of heaven

lines.text: As a false favourite doth his prince's name,
lines.plainText: As a false favourite doth his prince's name

lines.text: In deeds dishonourable? You have ta'en up,
lines.plainText: In deeds dishonourable You have ta'en up

lines.text: Under the counterfeited zeal of God,
lines.plainText: Under the counterfeited zeal of God

lines.text: The subjects of his substitute, my father,
lines.plainText: The subjects of his substitute my father

lines.text: And both against the peace of heaven and him
lines.plainText: And both against the peace of heaven and him

lines.text: Have here up-swarm'd them.
lines.plainText: Have here upswarm'd them

lines.text: Good my Lord of Lancaster,
lines.plainText: Good my Lord of Lancaster

lines.text: I am not here against your father's peace;
lines.plainText: I am not here against your father's peace

lines.text: But, as I told my Lord of Westmoreland,
lines.plainText: But as I told my Lord of Westmoreland

lines.text: The time misorder'd doth, in common sense,
lines.plainText: The time misorder'd doth in common sense

lines.text: Crowd us and crush us to this monstrous form
lines.plainText: Crowd us and crush us to this monstrous form

lines.text: To hold our safety up. I sent your Grace
lines.plainText: To hold our safety up I sent your Grace

lines.text: The parcels and particulars of our grief,
lines.plainText: The parcels and particulars of our grief

lines.text: The which hath been with scorn shoved from the court,
lines.plainText: The which hath been with scorn shoved from the court

lines.text: Whereon this Hydra son of war is born,
lines.plainText: Whereon this Hydra son of war is born

lines.text: Whose dangerous eyes may well be charm'd asleep
lines.plainText: Whose dangerous eyes may well be charm'd asleep

lines.text: With grant of our most just and right desires,
lines.plainText: With grant of our most just and right desires

lines.text: And true obedience, of this madness cured,
lines.plainText: And true obedience of this madness cured

lines.text: Stoop tamely to the foot of majesty.
lines.plainText: Stoop tamely to the foot of majesty

lines.text: If not, we ready are to try our fortunes
lines.plainText: If not we ready are to try our fortunes

lines.text: To the last man.
lines.plainText: To the last man

lines.text: And though we here fall down,
lines.plainText: And though we here fall down

lines.text: We have supplies to second our attempt:
lines.plainText: We have supplies to second our attempt

lines.text: If they miscarry, theirs shall second them;
lines.plainText: If they miscarry theirs shall second them

lines.text: And so success of mischief shall be born,
lines.plainText: And so success of mischief shall be born

lines.text: And heir from heir shall hold this quarrel up
lines.plainText: And heir from heir shall hold this quarrel up

lines.text: Whiles England shall have generation.
lines.plainText: Whiles England shall have generation

lines.text: You are too shallow, Hastings, much too shallow,
lines.plainText: You are too shallow Hastings much too shallow

lines.text: To sound the bottom of the after-times.
lines.plainText: To sound the bottom of the aftertimes

lines.text: Pleaseth your Grace to answer them directly
lines.plainText: Pleaseth your Grace to answer them directly

lines.text: How far forth you do like their articles.
lines.plainText: How far forth you do like their articles

lines.text: I like them all, and do allow them well,
lines.plainText: I like them all and do allow them well

lines.text: And swear here, by the honour of my blood,
lines.plainText: And swear here by the honour of my blood

lines.text: My father's purposes have been mistook,
lines.plainText: My father's purposes have been mistook

lines.text: And some about him have too lavishly
lines.plainText: And some about him have too lavishly

lines.text: Wrested his meaning and authority.
lines.plainText: Wrested his meaning and authority

lines.text: My lord, these griefs shall be with speed redress'd;
lines.plainText: My lord these griefs shall be with speed redress'd

lines.text: Upon my soul, they shall. If this may please you,
lines.plainText: Upon my soul they shall If this may please you

lines.text: Discharge your powers unto their several counties,
lines.plainText: Discharge your powers unto their several counties

lines.text: As we will ours; and here between the armies
lines.plainText: As we will ours and here between the armies

lines.text: Let's drink together friendly and embrace,
lines.plainText: Let's drink together friendly and embrace

lines.text: That all their eyes may bear those tokens home
lines.plainText: That all their eyes may bear those tokens home

lines.text: Of our restored love and amity.
lines.plainText: Of our restored love and amity

lines.text: I take your princely word for these redresses.
lines.plainText: I take your princely word for these redresses

lines.text: I give it you, and will maintain my word;
lines.plainText: I give it you and will maintain my word

lines.text: And thereupon I drink unto your Grace.
lines.plainText: And thereupon I drink unto your Grace

lines.text: Go, captain, and deliver to the army
lines.plainText: Go captain and deliver to the army

lines.text: This news of peace. Let them have pay, and part.
lines.plainText: This news of peace Let them have pay and part

lines.text: I know it will please them. Hie thee, captain.
lines.plainText: I know it will please them Hie thee captain

lines.text: To you, my noble Lord of Westmoreland.
lines.plainText: To you my noble Lord of Westmoreland

lines.text: I pledge your Grace; and if you knew what pains
lines.plainText: I pledge your Grace and if you knew what pains

lines.text: I have bestow'd to breed this present peace,
lines.plainText: I have bestow'd to breed this present peace

lines.text: You would drink freely; but my love to ye
lines.plainText: You would drink freely but my love to ye

lines.text: Shall show itself more openly hereafter.
lines.plainText: Shall show itself more openly hereafter

lines.text: I do not doubt you.
lines.plainText: I do not doubt you

lines.text: I am glad of it.
lines.plainText: I am glad of it

lines.text: Health to my lord and gentle cousin, Mowbray.
lines.plainText: Health to my lord and gentle cousin Mowbray

lines.text: You wish me health in very happy season,
lines.plainText: You wish me health in very happy season

lines.text: For I am on the sudden something ill.
lines.plainText: For I am on the sudden something ill

lines.text: Against ill chances men are ever merry,
lines.plainText: Against ill chances men are ever merry

lines.text: But heaviness foreruns the good event.
lines.plainText: But heaviness foreruns the good event

lines.text: Therefore be merry, coz, since sudden sorrow
lines.plainText: Therefore be merry coz since sudden sorrow

lines.text: Serves to say thus, "Some good thing comes tomorrow."
lines.plainText: Serves to say thus Some good thing comes tomorrow

lines.text: Believe me, I am passing light in spirit.
lines.plainText: Believe me I am passing light in spirit

lines.text: So much the worse, if your own rule be true.
lines.plainText: So much the worse if your own rule be true

lines.text: The word of peace is render'd. Hark how they shout!
lines.plainText: The word of peace is render'd Hark how they shout

lines.text: This had been cheerful after victory.
lines.plainText: This had been cheerful after victory

lines.text: A peace is of the nature of a conquest;
lines.plainText: A peace is of the nature of a conquest

lines.text: For then both parties nobly are subdued,
lines.plainText: For then both parties nobly are subdued

lines.text: And neither party loser.
lines.plainText: And neither party loser

lines.text: Go, my lord.
lines.plainText: Go my lord

lines.text: And let our army be discharged too.
lines.plainText: And let our army be discharged too

lines.text: Go, good Lord Hastings,
lines.plainText: Go good Lord Hastings

lines.text: And, ere they be dismiss'd, let them march by.
lines.plainText: And ere they be dismiss'd let them march by

lines.text: I trust, lords, we shall lie tonight together.
lines.plainText: I trust lords we shall lie tonight together

lines.text: The leaders, having charge from you to stand,
lines.plainText: The leaders having charge from you to stand

lines.text: Will not go off until they hear you speak.
lines.plainText: Will not go off until they hear you speak

lines.text: They know their duties.
lines.plainText: They know their duties

lines.text: My lord, our army is dispersed already.
lines.plainText: My lord our army is dispersed already

lines.text: Like youthful steers unyoked, they take their courses
lines.plainText: Like youthful steers unyoked they take their courses

lines.text: East, west, north, south; or, like a school broke up,
lines.plainText: East west north south or like a school broke up

lines.text: Each hurries toward his home and sporting-place.
lines.plainText: Each hurries toward his home and sportingplace

lines.text: Good tidings, my Lord Hastings; for the which
lines.plainText: Good tidings my Lord Hastings for the which

lines.text: I do arrest thee, traitor, of high treason;
lines.plainText: I do arrest thee traitor of high treason

lines.text: And you, Lord Archbishop, and you, Lord Mowbray,
lines.plainText: And you Lord Archbishop and you Lord Mowbray

lines.text: Of capital treason I attach you both.
lines.plainText: Of capital treason I attach you both

lines.text: Is this proceeding just and honourable?
lines.plainText: Is this proceeding just and honourable

lines.text: Is your assembly so?
lines.plainText: Is your assembly so

lines.text: Will you thus break your faith?
lines.plainText: Will you thus break your faith

lines.text: I pawn'd thee none.
lines.plainText: I pawn'd thee none

lines.text: I promised you redress of these same grievances
lines.plainText: I promised you redress of these same grievances

lines.text: Whereof you did complain; which, by mine honour,
lines.plainText: Whereof you did complain which by mine honour

lines.text: I will perform with a most Christian care.
lines.plainText: I will perform with a most Christian care

lines.text: But for you, rebels, look to taste the due
lines.plainText: But for you rebels look to taste the due

lines.text: Meet for rebellion and such acts as yours.
lines.plainText: Meet for rebellion and such acts as yours

lines.text: Most shallowly did you these arms commence,
lines.plainText: Most shallowly did you these arms commence

lines.text: Fondly brought here and foolishly sent hence.
lines.plainText: Fondly brought here and foolishly sent hence

lines.text: Strike up our drums, pursue the scattr'd stray:
lines.plainText: Strike up our drums pursue the scattr'd stray

lines.text: God, and not we, hath safely fought today.
lines.plainText: God and not we hath safely fought today

lines.text: Some guard these traitors to the block of death,
lines.plainText: Some guard these traitors to the block of death

lines.text: Treason's true bed and yielder-up of breath.
